Why I'm trying to pause AI | Joseph Miller | TEDxUniversityofStAndrews
recentItems.description: Scientists are warning that AI is the greatest threat to human survival since the invention of nuclear weapons. This talk will explain the reasons why the creation of superhuman AI would be detrimental and what PauseAI and others are trying to do about it. Joseph Miller a PhD student in Machine Learning at the University of Oxford, he is also the founder of Pause AI which advocates for leaders to pause unsafe AI development until real safeguards are put into place. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Fingernails to Fishing | Tom Huynh | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
What if your passion could become more than a hobby -- what if it could become a career?

Tom Huynh shares how a winding journey from the nail industry to professional fishing taught him an unexpected lesson: great educators aren't defined by a classroom or a degree, but by their passion, expertise, and willingness to share what they know. His story challenges the idea that educators must stay at the bottom of the pay scale and offers a new way to think about turning knowledge into opportunity. I have been in the nail salon industry for over 20 years, and more recently took the professional walleye fishing world by storm by being one of the first to use the newest technology to win multiple pro events and championships.  I have taken what I have learned and developed the first ever online fishing curriculum to teach everything I am learning.  In one year, I have enrollees in more than 40 states and 20 countries. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: You are not your job | Celeste Bell | TEDxRaleigh
recentItems.description: What happens when your job becomes your identity? “You Are Not Your Job” explores the risks of tying our self-worth too closely to work and how hobbies, interests, and meaningful pursuits outside of our careers can help us build a stronger identity, navigate career change and job loss, and create a more fulfilling life beyond work. Celeste Bell is a former C-suite HR executive turned professor and researcher whose work focuses on identity, work, and resilience. She’s also a 70-time marathoner who has run on every continent and uses serious leisure as a live experiment in what it means to build a self that’s bigger than a job title. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Healing Power of Humor | Dr. Kristen Wynns | TEDxRaleigh
recentItems.description: What if humor is more than entertainment-and actually a tool for healing? Clinical psychologist and stand-up comedian Dr. Kristen Wynns explores how humor can help us create connection, cope with adversity, and build resilience. Drawing from psychology, her own unexpected journey into comedy, and deeply personal experiences, she reveals that a sense of humor isn’t just something you’re born with-it’s a skill we can strengthen. Her challenge: become a little less serious, a little more silly, and discover how laughter can change the way we move through life’s hardest moments. Dr. Kristen Wynns is a child and adolescent psychologist, founder of Wynns Family Psychology, and author of The No Wimpy Parenting Handbook, whose work has shaped parenting and youth mental health for over 25 years. A sought-after media expert, speaker, and stand-up comedian, she blends psychology and humor to help people build resilience, confidence, and meaningful connection. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The unplanned yes | Dr. Michelle Chambers-Rollins | TEDxRaleigh
recentItems.description: Stop waiting to feel ready. Discover how facing anxiety, fear, avoidance, and uncertainty creates the evidence that builds confidence, courage, resilience, and encourages personal growth, one unplanned yes at a time. Dr. Michelle Chambers-Rollins is a trauma-informed mental health clinician and professor at UNC–Chapel Hill whose work examines how anxiety quietly governs the choices we make. Drawing on civic training, public systems work, and her book Faith to Win, she challenges people to reclaim agency and move forward even when certainty is unavailable. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Bravest Act Gets No Likes | Logan Elliot | TEDxUniversityofStAndrews
recentItems.description: Exploring the motivation behind good deeds, Logan’s talk investigates how validation can distort our intentions. Logan contrasts his journey with validation against his grandfather, a World War II freedom fighter, who avoided praise, saying “anyone would have done it.” But not everyone did, and Logan unpacks why and what this contrast reveals about the true drivers of moral action. Logan Eliot is a recent graduate from the University of St Andrews with a degree in Economics and Sustainable Development. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Being in Your element  | Julie Brook | TEDxUniversityofStAndrews
recentItems.description:
Through her practice visual artist Julie Brook will explore the idea of what it is to be in our element.
Brook makes sculptural work outside responding directly to the landscape and materials to hand. She will speak about her experience of living on the uninhabited west coast of Jura and how this influences her practice today. Julie Brook is a visual artist who works predominantly outdoors on large scale sculptural work. Her work is directly influenced by the many unique environments she has worked in including the west coast of Jura, the uninhabited island of Mingulay as well as further afield in South West Libya, Syria and Namibia. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Brain changes in addiction | Professor Alexander Baldacchino | TEDxUniversityofStAndrews
recentItems.description: Excessive and chronic rewards trigger dopamine floods and replace natural rewards. This ''high jacking" of the reward circuit leads to interesting changes in motivation that will change how individuals prioritise everyday tasks, value relationships and their expectations of their immediate environments. What is the difference between a negative and a positive addiction? When does instant gratification and memory impairments become problematic? This TED x talk will explore some of these issues and help normalise the notion that addicted individuals were morally weak and/or genetically  predisposed to become dependent on psychoactive substances. Professor Baldacchino holds a variety of esteemed positions including Chair of the World Psychiatric Association (WPA) Addiction Faculty, Scientific Advisor for the European Union Drug Agency (EUDA) and World Health organisation (WHO). His main research interest lies in improving the lives of individuals with a history of substance use disorders and addictive behaviours. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Why I climbed 282 Scottish mountains | Jamie Aarons | TEDxUniversityofStAndrews
recentItems.description: What if the most powerful force in achieving something great isn’t certainty—but a sliver of possibility? In this inspiring talk, Jamie Aarons explores how extraordinary achievements often begin with a tiny spark she calls “The Glimmer of Maybe.” Sharing the story of her self‑propelled continuous Munro round, she reflects on being driven not by certainty but by the very real possibility of failure. Through storms, exhaustion, and with some incredibly sore feet, she demonstrated that resilience grows one choice at a time—and rarely alone. This talk highlights the power of community and tenacity, and invites audiences to rethink what’s possible when we let the mind lead the body, when we welcome the prospect of failure as a catalyst, and when we embrace the quiet but powerful idea that maybe—just maybe—something extraordinary could happen. Jamie Aarons is an enthusiastic adventure racer, ultra runner, cyclist and kayaker as well as a devoted social worker. In 2023, she embarked on a self propelled Munro challenge where she scaled 282 Scottish peaks over 3000 feat. Jamie finished the challenge in 31 days 10 hours and 27 minutes, thereby breaking the previous record. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Climate Brides | Dr Reetika Revathy Subramanian | TEDxUniversityofStAndrews
recentItems.description: In South Asia, climate change is not only reshaping coastlines and crops. It is redefining childhood. When floods, droughts, and heatwaves disrupt livelihoods, families are forced into impossible calculations. For some, marrying a daughter early becomes a way to manage risk, secure support, or enable mobility. Not simply tradition, but survival shaped by shrinking choices. Masculinities, too, are being renegotiated, as work disappears and expectations remain. Drawing on stories and research from the Climate Brides project, this talk reveals how climate shocks remake family life, gender roles, and the bargains through which child marriage is recast as survival. Ultimately, climate justice is about whose futures are protected, and whose are negotiated away in a warming world. Dr Subramanian is a Senior Research associate and BBC- AHRC New Generation Thinker 2025 who works in the School of Global Development at the University of East Anglia. Her work focuses on climate change, gender and labour migration. She is the creator of the Climate Brides podcast. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
